summary.title: FIT5163 Week 8 Lab
summary.description: MediTrack lab threat model: patients, doctors and administrators use a Web/API server for appointments and medical records. Reminders use a third-party SMS provider. Includes TB1-TB5 and the 10 worked STRIDE threats from the supplied lab. Controls are proposals, not implemented assurances. The supplied component-level threat list has been added. New priorities are TBD pending risk assessment; all new threats remain Open. Existing threat entries and diagram geometry are preserved.

data.name: TB4 - Third party

TB1 - Internet / API
data.description: Untrusted browser requests enter the Web/API server. Authenticate, validate and authorise. Responses cross back to the browser. The full-height line separates the labelled zones and covers all related cross-boundary flows.

data.name: TB5 - Role / object checks
data.description: Logical privilege boundary inside the same Web/API server, not a network segment. Check Patient/Doctor/Admin permissions and object-level access for every action. The full-height line separates the labelled zones and covers all related cross-boundary flows.

data.name: Patient
data.description: Patient browser. Log in, book/cancel appointments and view own medical records. Browser input is untrusted.

threats.title: Patient impersonation using compromised credentials
threats.description: An attacker uses leaked or phished patient credentials to sign in as the patient and access personal records or appointment functions.
threats.mitigation: Offer MFA, screen passwords against known compromised passwords, protect login transport and monitor suspicious sign-ins. Revoke compromised sessions and provide a secure account-recovery process.

threats.title: Patient denies booking or cancelling an appointment
threats.description: A patient denies creating or cancelling an appointment when the system lacks a trustworthy record of the authenticated request and outcome.
threats.mitigation: Audit appointment creation and cancellation with actor, appointment ID, timestamp and outcome; retain protected change history and send confirmations without unnecessary sensitive data.

data.name: Doctor
data.description: Doctor browser. Access authorised patient records; create or update notes and prescriptions.

threats.title: Doctor account impersonation via stolen credentials
threats.description: An attacker who obtains a Doctor's stolen or phished credentials (e.g. via phishing, credential leak, or weak password) can log in as that Doctor via the Web/API Authentication process, gaining unauthorized access to patient medical records, prescriptions, and appointment data.
threats.mitigation: Enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA) for Doctor accounts; implement account lockout after repeated failed login attempts; monitor for logins from unusual IP addresses or devices; enforce strong password policy.

threats.title: Doctor denies viewing or modifying a medical record
threats.description: A doctor denies accessing or changing a patient record. Without reliable audit evidence linking the authenticated doctor to the action, the organisation cannot establish who accessed or altered the record.
threats.mitigation: Record the authenticated actor, record ID, action, timestamp, outcome and change version for each read/write. Protect audit logs against alteration and restrict access; avoid copying full health records into logs.

data.name: Admin
data.description: Receptionist/admin browser. Manage schedules and user accounts through the API; no direct store access or blanket medical-record access is assumed.

threats.title: Admin impersonation using stolen credentials
threats.description: An attacker steals an administrator credential and uses administrative functions to change accounts or schedules maliciously.
threats.mitigation: Require MFA for administrators, separate administrative accounts, restrict privileged access, alert on unusual administrative logins and promptly revoke compromised credentials and sessions.

threats.title: Admin denies configuration or schedule changes
threats.description: An administrator denies changing schedules or available system configuration, and missing audit records prevent attribution. Configuration changes apply only where such administrative functionality exists.
threats.mitigation: Maintain tamper-protected audit logs of administrative changes, including actor, target, timestamp, before/after values and outcome. Require individual administrator accounts and review privileged activity.

data.name:
Web / API
Authentication
Input validation
data.description: Logical entry component of the single Web/API server. Validates all browser input and sessions at TB1. The second process is an internal decomposition, not a separate deployed server.

threats.title: Credential stuffing or brute-force login
threats.description: An attacker submits stolen credential pairs or repeated password guesses to the login endpoint to impersonate legitimate users.
threats.mitigation: Use MFA, compromised-password screening, per-account and per-source rate limits, progressive delays and suspicious-login detection. Avoid unlimited lockouts that allow attackers to deny access to victims.

threats.title: Session cookie manipulation enables session hijacking
threats.description: An attacker alters a session identifier or client-controlled claims. If session validation fails to enforce integrity and a server-side identity binding, the modified cookie may be accepted as another user session.
threats.mitigation: Use opaque unpredictable session IDs validated against trusted server-side state, or verify signed token integrity and claims. Reject modified or unknown identifiers, rotate tokens at login/privilege changes and set Secure, HttpOnly and appropriate SameSite cookie attributes.

threats.title: Authentication events lack an audit trail
threats.description: Missing login and session-creation audit events prevent investigation or attribution of suspicious successful and failed authentication attempts.
threats.mitigation: Log authentication successes/failures, session issuance/revocation, account identifier, timestamp and relevant source context. Protect and monitor logs; never record passwords or usable session tokens.

threats.title: Login errors reveal whether an account exists
threats.description: Different error messages, response codes or response timing disclose whether a username or email address is registered, enabling user enumeration.
threats.mitigation: Return consistent public messages and response behaviour for invalid usernames and passwords. Reduce timing differences, rate-limit attempts and keep detailed diagnostics in protected internal logs.

threats.title: Login request flooding exhausts authentication resources
threats.description: An attacker floods the login endpoint, exhausting password-hashing capacity, database connections or request workers and preventing legitimate sign-ins.
threats.mitigation: Apply bounded request queues, per-account/per-source rate limits, global capacity limits, timeouts and monitoring. Limit concurrent password verification while preserving secure password hashing.

threats.title: Untrusted role binding during session creation
threats.description: The server trusts a client-supplied role or fails to verify the account-role relationship when creating a session, allowing a patient to receive doctor or administrator privileges.
threats.mitigation: Derive roles from authoritative server-side account records, ignore client role claims, enforce least privilege and revalidate permissions after role changes. Rotate or revoke affected sessions.

data.privilegeLevel: Server-side least privilege; per-request role and object checks required

data.name:
Web / API
Booking, records
and messaging
data.description: Internal application functions of the same Web/API server. TB5 requires role and object authorisation on every action. Patient: own data; doctor: treating relationship; admin: schedules/accounts. Deny by default.

threats.title: Stored XSS or permissive CORS
threats.description: A malicious stored note/message can act in a doctor session; permissive credentialed CORS may expose the records API. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Apply contextual output encoding and CSP; use a strict CORS allow-list and never reflect arbitrary credentialed origins.

threats.title: Booking or API resource exhaustion
threats.description: Unbounded requests or bookings exhaust appointment slots or server resources. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use rate limits, per-account booking quotas and bounded execution timeouts.

threats.title: Unauthorised modification of another patient appointment
threats.description: A user changes an appointment identifier or owner field and modifies or cancels another patient appointment when ownership checks are missing.
threats.mitigation: Enforce object-level authorisation on every update/cancellation, bind appointment ownership server-side, allow-list editable fields and apply transaction/concurrency controls.

threats.title: Record access and updates are not traceable
threats.description: The application reads or writes clinical records without an auditable link between the authenticated user, target record and operation, preventing reliable investigation of disputed actions.
threats.mitigation: Audit sensitive reads and all changes with actor, record ID, action, timestamp, outcome and version. Use append-only or tamper-evident storage with restricted access and monitored retention.

threats.title: IDOR exposes another patient medical record
threats.description: An attacker guesses or obtains another record ID and retrieves its contents because the endpoint does not verify ownership or the treating-clinician relationship. Predictable IDs aid discovery; missing authorisation causes the exposure.
threats.mitigation: Check permission on each requested record and field server-side. Deny by default, restrict bulk access and minimise returned fields; unpredictable identifiers are only an additional defence.

threats.title: Abusive bulk queries exhaust application resources
threats.description: An attacker repeatedly requests large record or appointment result sets, consuming CPU, memory and database capacity and delaying legitimate requests.
threats.mitigation: Enforce pagination, maximum page size, per-user query quotas, query timeouts and bounded concurrency. Restrict expensive filters and bulk export functions to authorised users.

threats.title: TB5 role or object checks are bypassed
threats.description: An attacker reaches a protected booking, clinical or administrative action through an endpoint or code path that omits the TB5 role/object permission check.
threats.mitigation: Centralise authorisation and enforce it on every protected path. Verify roles and the specific object relationship server-side, deny unknown actions by default and validate negative permission cases.

data.privilegeLevel: Server-side least privilege; per-request role and object checks required

data.name:
Patients +
Appointments DB
data.description: Patient/account data and appointment schedules. DB queries must be parameterised at TB2. Encryption and credential-storage controls are requirements, not verified implemented controls.

threats.title: Password disclosure from database leak
threats.description: A leaked database reveals plaintext passwords or easily cracked fast hashes. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use salted Argon2id/scrypt/bcrypt hashes; encrypt sensitive data at rest and restrict database access.

threats.title: Unauthorised direct database writes
threats.description: An attacker with stolen database credentials or exposed database access bypasses the application and changes patient accounts or appointment data directly.
threats.mitigation: Restrict database connectivity to approved services, apply least-privileged database roles, protect/rotate credentials and monitor privileged writes. Use integrity constraints, change monitoring and recoverable backups.

threats.title: Database operations lack audit evidence
threats.description: Database changes cannot be attributed to a responsible service or administrator because database audit records are absent or editable by the same principal.
threats.mitigation: Enable appropriate database audit logging and correlate service activity with application request IDs. Use individual privileged identities and forward protected logs to a separately controlled destination.

threats.title: Unencrypted data at rest exposes patient information
threats.description: Unauthorised access to database files, storage snapshots or backups reveals patient and appointment information when data at rest is unencrypted.
threats.mitigation: Encrypt database storage, snapshots and backups; manage keys separately with restricted access. Protect database credentials and hash passwords with a salted slow password KDF; encryption does not replace access control.

threats.title: Database connection pool exhaustion
threats.description: Slow or malicious requests occupy all available database connections, preventing legitimate account and appointment operations.
threats.mitigation: Bound connection pools and request concurrency, set query/transaction timeouts, release connections reliably, optimise expensive queries and rate-limit abusive callers.

data.name:
Medical records
store
data.description: Critical asset: patient health records, clinical notes and prescriptions. Every object read/write requires authorisation at TB3. Record changes require protected audit evidence.

threats.title: Malicious changes to diagnoses or prescriptions
threats.description: An unauthorised user or compromised service modifies diagnosis or prescription records, undermining clinical integrity and potentially affecting patient care.
threats.mitigation: Enforce per-record and action-level authorisation, least-privileged write access, protected version history and tamper-evident audit trails. Validate changes and support controlled recovery.

threats.title: Protected health information is disclosed
threats.description: An attacker or unauthorised insider obtains sensitive health records through compromised storage access, exposed backups or excessive permissions.
threats.mitigation: Restrict access by role and patient-care relationship, encrypt records and backups, isolate key management and monitor unusual reads/exports. Return only necessary fields and review access regularly.

threats.title: Doctor denies issuing or changing a prescription
threats.description: A doctor denies issuing or editing a prescription and the record store lacks protected provenance and version history linking the change to an authenticated identity.
threats.mitigation: Preserve attributable prescription versions and tamper-protected audit events with author, timestamp, action and outcome. Require reauthentication for sensitive signing actions where appropriate.

data.name:
SMS provider
(third party)
data.description: External provider delivering appointment reminders to patients. Send only the phone number and minimum reminder details; never full medical records.

threats.title: Patient phone numbers are exposed to a third party
threats.description: Sending reminders exposes patient phone numbers and any included appointment information to the SMS provider, whose access, retention or onward disclosure may exceed the intended purpose.
threats.mitigation: Send only the minimum recipient and reminder information; exclude diagnosis and clinical record content. Use TLS, agree retention/deletion and access requirements, and review provider handling.

threats.title: Spoofed or hijacked SMS gateway sends phishing messages
threats.description: An attacker impersonates the SMS gateway or compromises its API credentials/account and sends messages that appear to originate from the healthcare service.
threats.mitigation: Validate gateway TLS certificates and endpoint identity, protect and rotate API credentials, restrict provider permissions and monitor message destinations/content. Keep reminders free of requests for passwords or sensitive replies.

threats.title: SMS provider outage prevents appointment reminders
threats.description: A third-party outage, API throttling or delivery failure prevents reminders from reaching patients even when the core booking service is available.
threats.mitigation: Queue reminders with bounded retries/backoff, monitor delivery failures and use a circuit breaker. Provide an approved fallback communication channel where available and keep booking operations independent of SMS availability.

data.name: Session store
data.description: Server-side session IDs, user identity and expiry. Session data must be integrity-protected; tokens require strong randomness and controlled expiry.

threats.title: Session fixation persists an attacker-chosen identifier
threats.description: An attacker arranges for a victim to use a session identifier known to the attacker. If login keeps that identifier and binds it to the victim, the attacker can reuse the authenticated session.
threats.mitigation: Generate a new unpredictable session ID after login and privilege changes, invalidate the old ID, reject unissued identifiers and avoid accepting session IDs in URLs. Bind sessions to authoritative server-side identity state.

threats.title: Compromised session storage enables mass impersonation
threats.description: An attacker reads usable session identifiers or secrets from the session store and reuses them to impersonate many logged-in users.
threats.mitigation: Isolate and restrict the session store, encrypt sensitive storage and transport, avoid retaining reusable raw tokens where a one-way token lookup is sufficient, enforce short lifetimes and support rapid bulk revocation.

threats.title: Mass session creation exhausts session storage
threats.description: An attacker repeatedly creates sessions, filling the store or exhausting memory and preventing legitimate session creation or validation.
threats.mitigation: Enforce session TTLs, automatic expiry cleanup, per-account/per-source creation limits and bounded storage capacity. Monitor growth and limit unnecessary anonymous sessions.

data.name:
Login / book / cancel / view own records
Session cookie and responses
data.description: Patient requests and corresponding responses. Encryption flags are not asserted because transport controls have not been verified.

threats.title: Session spoofing
threats.description: Stolen or guessable session cookies allow impersonation of a patient or doctor. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Use CSPRNG session tokens, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, expiry and rotation; consider MFA.

threats.title: CSRF books or cancels appointments
threats.description: A forged cross-site request changes a booking using the victim session. Initial severity is a proposed qualitative assessment for review; likelihood and deployment details are not verified.
threats.mitigation: Require anti-CSRF tokens on state-changing requests and appropriate SameSite cookies.

threats.mitigation: Use parameterised queries/prepared statements and least-privileged database credentials.

diagrams.description: MediTrack DFD. The two Web/API process symbols decompose one server logically. TB1: Internet/API; TB2: database; TB3: records; TB4: SMS provider; TB5: role and object authorisation inside the API. No direct admin-to-database access is assumed. All threats remain Open; severity estimates require review. Revised: larger bidirectional arrowheads on seven request/response flows; SMS remains unidirectional. Authentication ports are separated to avoid overlapping arrowheads. TB1 and TB5 extend across the full working height and zones are labelled; authentication is not a guarantee that input is safe.
